name: HELIOS (NA34/2)
notes: Identity: HELIOS is the CERN experiment NA34. Hedberg's HELIOS page says it 'consisted of two fixed-target experiments at the SPS' (NA34/2, heavy ions; NA34/1, lepton production in hadronic interactions); Greybook lists NA34/2 with the synonym IONS/HELIOS (title 'Study of High Energy Densities over Extended Nuclear Volumes via Nucleus-Nucleus Collisions at the SPS'); Schukraft and Stock (arXiv:1505.06853) say NA34 'became NA34-2'. The acronym is expanded as High Energy Lepton and Ion Spectrometer in the 1991 Czech. J. Phys. abstract. This record is the heavy-ion part (NA34/2, 'HELIOS-2'); the proton-beam lepton-production part (NA34/1, 'HELIOS-1') shares the apparatus and collaboration.

Related but not recorded: HELIOS-3 (NA34/3, Greybook: 'Measurement of Low Mass Muon Pairs in Sulphur-Nucleus Collisions with an Optimized HELIOS Muon Spectrometer', approved 10 November 1988), the dimuon experiment that found the low-mass dimuon excess (Tserruya, arXiv:nucl-ex/9801007). It is a separate approved experiment and was not in the brief; listed for the integrator.
Hall not identified: placed at the generic Prévessin North Area site (Greybook: beam H8).

No collaboration website found (Greybook lists none). Heavy-ion papers of the HELIOS Collaboration are not on arXiv; the sources are Greybook, the Hedberg pages, Specht's 2014 slides and the 1988 and 1991 journal abstracts.
CERES split off from HELIOS-3 to design a dedicated electron-pair experiment (arXiv:2603.10835, Section 3.1); no lineage row was written because that is a group split, not a predecessor relation.
INSPIRE experiment id not looked up: inspirehep.net is off-limits to coverage streams (STREAM_RULES); external.inspire_experiment left null for the integrator.

summary.plain: HELIOS was a CERN experiment that sent oxygen and sulphur ions into heavy targets and surrounded the target with calorimeters to measure how much energy sprayed sideways. It found energy densities near those where lattice QCD expects quarks and gluons to be freed.
summary.technical: HELIOS (NA34/2): almost 4-pi uranium-scintillator calorimetry with silicon detectors, a hadron spectrometer, photon (NaI) and dimuon (NA3 spectrometer) measurements, on the H8 beam line of the SPS North Area; O and S beams at 60A and 200A GeV and proton beams; transverse-energy and multiplicity distributions (energy density near the lattice-QCD deconfinement value of about 2.5 GeV/fm3), photon spectra consistent with hadronic sources, kaon production.
